clips.text_zh: Tesla 今日無端端跌11%，成個公司根本係一個 meme。之前成日睇Tesla同Musk，廢柴都開始覺得，搏Mood唔係工程力學。
clips.text_en_b1: Tesla crashed 11% for no fucking reason. The entire company is a meme. This is exactly the kind of market nonsense that makes me understand why my CFD losses keep looking like tuition.
clips.text_en_b2: Tesla crashed 11% for absolutely no apparent reason, which makes the whole company look like a meme to me. This is precisely the sort of market nonsense that makes me understand why my CFD losses keep looking like tuition. I used to follow Tesla and Musk regularly, but even a useless engineer can tell that chasing the mood is no substitute for actual engineering. The numbers speak for themselves, and they are hardly impressive.
clips.text_en_c1: Tesla crashed 11% for absolutely no fucking reason, which makes the entire company look like a meme. This is precisely the sort of market nonsense that makes me understand why my CFD losses keep appearing like tuition rather than an inevitable financial burden. For years, people watched Musk and Tesla as if they were serious technological enterprises; now even the idiots are beginning to suspect that manipulating sentiment has replaced engineering, physics, and competent decision-making. If fundamentals cannot explain an 11% plunge, then the market is pricing theatre, not performance, and my trading fees remain the tax for an expensive education.
clips.text_en_c2: Tesla has crashed by 11 percent for absolutely no discernible reason, which makes the whole enterprise look less like a serious technology company and more like an elaborate financial meme. Earlier, watching Tesla and Musk repeatedly proved enough that even a clueless observer began to suspect that pandering to the mood of the market had displaced engineering, physics, and any coherent notion of risk. This is precisely the sort of market theatre that makes my own CFD losses look less like financial education and more like tuition paid to the market for the privilege of being repeatedly wrong. The numbers speak for themselves; the reasoning behind them appears to have been outsourced to the zeitgeist.
clips.source_hint: A /biz/ post about Tesla's unexplained 11% crash.

clips.text_zh: 由Bot Usage開始睇。Musk 突然 cut usage of their most popular product by 60%，仲要無通知就cut。X同Reddit而家 seethe 得好似Trump第一次當選。Musk troll of the year啦，wtf，佢到底有咩endgame？
clips.text_en_b1: From Bot Usage: Elon Musk cut usage to their most popular product by 60 percent for paying subscribers, with no notice. People on X and Reddit are now seething almost as intensely as when President Trump was first elected. I vote for Musk as troll of the year. What is his endgame?
clips.text_en_b2: From Bot Usage: Elon Musk cut usage to their most popular product by 60% for paying subscribers, without giving any notice. People on X and Reddit are now seething almost as intensely as they did when President Trump was first elected. I vote for Musk as troll of the year, although his motives remain completely opaque. What exactly is his endgame here, and why does he keep treating loyal customers as if they are disposable?
clips.text_en_c1: According to Bot Usage, Elon Musk cut usage limits for their most popular product by 60% for paying subscribers, apparently without any notice. The result is that people on X and Reddit are now seething almost as intensely as they did when President Trump was first elected. I vote for Musk as troll of the year, although I am still trying to work out what his endgame actually is. What strategic benefit could such a transparently hostile decision produce? Unless the purpose was simply to provoke a mass reaction, it seems more like a calculated insult than a serious product strategy.
clips.text_en_c2: The latest development comes courtesy of Bot Usage: Elon Musk has abruptly cut usage limits for X, apparently the platform’s most popular paid product, by 60 percent, and subscribers received no advance warning whatsoever. Users on both X and Reddit are now seething with roughly the collective fury that accompanied Donald Trump’s first election, which is an appreciable achievement for a platform whose culture has historically regarded outrage as a form of social participation. I personally nominate Musk as troll of the year, although the competition may prove unexpectedly stiff. The strategic rationale is opaque, and the execution is careless; what precisely, in his estimation, constitutes the endgame?
clips.source_hint: A /biz/ thread about Musk cutting bot usage and the resulting backlash.

clips.text_zh: Musk又chimps out。有人指出，vacuum of space係insulator，對data centers唔係好事，佢就鬧人。靠AI續命civil engineer今日表示：連基本物理都唔trusted，AI data center會唔會由HyperAI先死？
clips.text_en_b1: Musk chimps out at a man pointing out that the vacuum of space is an insulator, which is bad for data centers. Is it really a good idea to trust our tech sector and immigration policies to someone who clearly does not know what he is talking about? He also ignored basic facts and logic.
clips.text_en_b2: Musk chimped out at a man who pointed out that the vacuum of space is an insulator, making it a bad environment for data centers. Is it really sensible to trust our technology sector and immigration policies to someone who clearly does not understand what he is talking about? He also ignored basic facts and logic, which is hardly reassuring. If AI data centers have to operate in space, perhaps HyperAI will be the first to die.
clips.text_en_c1: Musk chimps out at a man who points out that the vacuum of space is an insulator, which is bad for data centers. This raises an obvious question: is it sensible to trust our technology sector, not to mention immigration policy, to someone who evidently does not understand what he is talking about? He ignores basic facts and elementary logic while dismissing the person raising a legitimate technical concern. If space-based data centers are going to become a serious business, then the physics of heat dissipation cannot be treated as an inconvenience to be overridden through confidence, rhetoric, or personal hostility.
clips.text_en_c2: Musk has chimps out again, this time after someone pointed out that the vacuum of space functions as an insulator, which is hardly advantageous for the proposed data centres in orbit. Instead of engaging with the physics, he resorts to berating the person who raised it. Is it genuinely prudent to entrust our technology sector, our infrastructure ambitions, and even our immigration policies to a man who appears not to understand the fundamental properties of the environment he intends to exploit? Musk ignored not merely inconvenient details but basic facts, elementary logic, and the scientific principles that ought to govern any credible discussion of orbital computation.
clips.source_hint: A /g/ discussion about Musk, space physics, data centers, and public subsidies.

clips.text_zh: It’s already happening。香港新聞版又見到Musk個名，post只係問：點解Elon loser Muskrat feel點？廢物連新聞都係conflict，睇完只想返去trade，睇吓個prop firm仲有幾多P&L。
clips.text_en_b1: It is already happening. How is Elon loser Muskrat feeling? The post gives no further context, but the key name is Elon Musk, and the question is already turning into another political pile-on.
clips.text_en_b2: It is already happening. A Hong Kong news post has somehow featured Musk’s name again, asking how “Elon loser Muskrat” is feeling and offering no further context. The important detail is that Elon Musk is involved, so the question has immediately turned into another political pile-on. After reading it, I just want to go back to trading and check how much profit and loss my proprietary trading firm still has left.
clips.text_en_c1: It is already happening: Elon Musk has appeared again in the Hong Kong news section, and the post simply asks how Elon, the loser Muskrat, is feeling. No further context is provided, yet the crucial name alone is enough to turn the story into another political pile-on. Musk seems to generate conflict even when the article contains no obvious political substance whatsoever. Watching this circus makes me want to return to trading and check how much P&L remains at the prop firm, rather than waste any more time on a manufactured dispute engineered for attention and public outrage.
clips.text_en_c2: It is already happening, as though the principal objective of political discourse were to drag every controversy into the orbit of Elon Musk. A Hong Kong news feed has once again surfaced his name in a post that asks, with commendable brevity, how “Elon loser Muskrat” is feeling today. No substantive context is supplied; no argument is developed, and no verifiable claim is offered to illuminate the matter. The absence of information merely makes the question function as an open invitation to political pile-on, in which every participant may append his preferred insult while appearing to contribute to a debate nobody had actually begun. I read it, felt briefly sorry for everyone involved, and then went back to trading to see how much profit and loss remained at the prop firm.
clips.source_hint: A short /pol/ post about Elon Musk and political news.

clips.text_zh: 有人問，要lift幾多重先可以抵消畫anime呢個cringe hobby？佢做gym、indoor bouldering、run，仲讀accounting，有正常朋友，但一直唔敢同人講自己畫anime。廢柴工程師睇完覺得，咁又係一條load path：個voxel更加唔敢出口。
clips.text_en_b1: How much do you need to lift to offset a cringe hobby like drawing anime? The poster hits the gym, does indoor bouldering, runs for cardio, studies accounting, and has an okay friend group. However, they love drawing anime and have never revealed it to anyone.
clips.text_en_b2: Someone asked how much weight they need to lift to offset a cringe hobby such as drawing anime. The poster works out, does indoor bouldering, runs for cardio, studies accounting, and has a decent group of friends. Nevertheless, they love drawing anime and have never told anyone about it. It is a strange kind of load path: the more you improve physically, the less courage you seem to have to admit what you actually enjoy.
clips.text_en_c1: How much weight would somebody need to lift to offset having a cringe hobby such as drawing anime? The poster goes to the gym, does indoor bouldering, runs for cardio, and studies accounting; they also have a perfectly decent circle of friends. Nevertheless, they love drawing anime and have never told anyone about it. As an engineering loser, I can only conclude that this is another load path: every additional rep may increase the structure's capacity, but it does nothing to stop the shame from propagating. The real problem is not physical weakness; it is social vulnerability and the irrational fear of embarrassment.
clips.text_en_c2: The poster wonders how much weight one would have to lift to counterbalance the social cost of a supposedly cringe hobby such as drawing anime. Their defence is almost suspiciously comprehensive: they visit the gym, practise indoor bouldering, run for cardiovascular conditioning, study accounting, and maintain an entirely respectable circle of friends. Nevertheless, they love drawing anime and have never disclosed this private enthusiasm to anybody, which suggests that the hobby remains inseparable from embarrassment in their own mind. As an engineer, I recognise the underlying structural problem: if every additional rep can only reinforce the façade while the concealed source of shame remains untouched, then the load path is badly designed, and there is no amount of muscular effort capable of resolving it.
clips.source_hint: A /fit/ thread about lifting, social confidence, and drawing anime.

clips.text_zh: 有人話，coding by hand、drawing by hand、write your own texts、model by hand、compose songs、do your own research，全部畀AI obsolete。咁樣大部分人只識delegate，腦就rot to mush。睇完真係靠AI續命，連睇Gundam 00都要AI幫我做summary。
clips.text_en_b1: All of these are made obsolete by AI: coding by hand, drawing by hand, writing your own texts, modelling by hand, composing songs, doing your own research, and reading books or articles past the headline. People delegate everything to AI and rot their brains to mush.
clips.text_en_b2: AI is supposedly making all of these obsolete: coding by hand, drawing by hand, writing your own texts, modelling by hand, composing songs, doing your own research, and reading books or articles beyond the headline. Once most people delegate everything to AI, their brains will rot to mush. Honestly, I rely on AI to keep me going, even when watching Gundam 00, because I need it to summarize what is happening.
clips.text_en_c1: According to the poster, AI has made all of these activities obsolete: coding by hand, drawing by hand, writing your own texts, modelling by hand, composing songs, conducting your own research, and reading books or articles beyond the headline. If most people simply delegate everything to AI, their brains will rot to mush because none of the underlying skills are ever practised. This is allegedly how I am surviving, since even watching Gundam 00 now requires AI to prepare a summary for me. The convenience is obvious, but so is the deeper danger: once intellectual effort becomes optional, ordinary competence gradually disappears.
clips.text_en_c2: According to the argument in question, AI has rendered a long catalogue of human activities obsolete: coding by hand, drawing by hand, writing original texts, constructing mathematical models manually, composing songs, conducting independent research, and even reading books or articles beyond the headline. The implied conclusion is that, once everyone delegates virtually every cognitive task to the machine, the human brain will gradually rot into cognitive mush. There is some irony in a profession whose survival strategy currently depends on AI to identify the relevant source material, because even summarising Gundam 00 now apparently requires assistance. Rather than confidently absorbing information, we risk outsourcing not merely the labour of thought but the willingness to think at all.
clips.source_hint: A /g/ thread about AI making original skills seem obsolete.
